mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during a recovery phase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during a broader economic downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal that often precedes a downward revision in labor market expectations; this ambiguity increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during clear labor market expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Retail Sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth expectations for consumer-facing sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 6-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below the median baseline at 95% confidence.
